headline: Open-source AI turns handwritten bills into profit intelligence for small eateries, offering 10x ROI
summary: PaperToProfit, a mobile-first, privacy-preserving engine, digitizes handwritten restaurant bills in seconds, providing real-time revenue, profit, and inventory insights for local diners and dhabas. It aims to prevent food waste and revenue leakage.
details: Small eateries in South Asia often track orders on handwritten paper slips, leading to hours of manual reconciliation and a lack of real-time financial insights. Commercial POS systems are often too expensive and complex for these businesses.

PaperToProfit offers a mobile-first, privacy-preserving solution designed specifically for neighborhood food businesses. It digitizes handwritten or printed bills using a camera or copy-paste, parsing items, prices, and categories with confidence scores.

The system provides real-time gross revenue, estimated net profit, food costs, average ticket size, and 14-day revenue trajectory. It also categorizes dishes into "Stars," "Plowhorses," "Puzzles," and "Dogs" based on sales volume and profit margins.

Leveraging Prior Labs' TabPFN-3.5 foundation model, PaperToProfit forecasts next-week revenue with confidence bounds and flags anomalous revenue spikes or drops. This helps provide actionable prep recommendations.

The project emphasizes a strict philosophy of zero-latency local execution, resilient multi-engine fallbacks, and zero proprietary lock-in. All verified slips are recorded in a local SQLite ledger with 1-click CSV export for accounting.

Reading faded carbon copies and cursive handwriting is challenging for traditional OCR. PaperToProfit uses a 3-tier cascade for robust parsing. The complete source code is open-source under the MIT license.

The open-source approach addresses crucial needs for small businesses, including data privacy (financial records never leave premises) and customization for regional handwritten slang. Closed models often struggle with such nuances.

The developer built this project, including FastAPI architecture and TabPFN integration, with assistance from Antigravity. A personal anecdote highlights its effectiveness, showing it parsed a real, messy handwritten bill in under 2 seconds.

topic: pgpool-ii client certificate validation bypass vulnerability
headline_marked: [[Pgpool-II client cert validation bypass]] (CVE-2026-92868) affects many versions
headline: Pgpool-II client cert validation bypass (CVE-2026-92868) affects many versions
summary: A critical flaw, CVE-2026-92868, allows client certificate authentication bypass in Pgpool-II. It impacts versions from 3.5.x up to 4.7.2, requiring immediate patching.
details: The Pgpool Global Development Group has released fixes for a critical client certificate validation bypass, CVE-2026-92868. This flaw, classified as CWE-295, has a CVSS v4 base score of 6.9.
It affects Pgpool-II versions from 3.5.x up to 4.7.2, meaning a large share of installed clusters are vulnerable. The issue allows client certificate authentication to be bypassed.
The vulnerability impacts Pgpool-II versions from 3.5.x up to 4.7.2. Fixed releases include 4.7.3, 4.6.8, 4.5.13, 4.4.18, and 4.3.21 across maintained branches.

The flaw stems from an improper implementation of the client certificate check, turning the validation step into a weak point. Its practical severity depends on whether TLS with client certificate authentication is enabled in a deployment.

Six other CVEs were also addressed, including four memory safety issues. CVE-2026-92867 allows arbitrary code execution with low privilege, while CVE-2026-92873 enables arbitrary watchdog node promotion.

Identifying affected clusters can be challenging, as distributions and container images might package older minor releases. Administrators should verify the running binary version directly rather than relying on package listings.
It is crucial to update to the latest patched versions: 4.7.3, 4.6.8, 4.5.13, 4.4.18, and 4.3.21. Clusters on 4.2.x or older require a branch upgrade, as these EOL versions will not receive patches.
